manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

Walls: R1C5 R1C6 R1C7 R1C8 R2C2 R3C2 R3C5 R3C6 R3C7 R3C8 R4C4 R5C3 R6C3 R6C7 R7C5 R7C6

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading?    PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.

   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: done

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.

- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

- You may only move objects you control.

Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">

- You may only move objects you control.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.

   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.

   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, D, E. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a message. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammate's situation: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammate.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed
